meta.ogDescription: Yes — Robbins wrote it in Awaken the Giant Within (1991). Wikiquote's sourced section cites page 75.

answer.label: Written by

answer.sourceLine: This one is genuinely his. Wikiquote’s sourced section for Awaken the Giant Within prints the sentence and cites page 75, where it opens a longer thought that runs on: “Human beings have the awesome ability to take any experience of their lives and create a meaning that disempowers them or one that can literally save their lives.” The book was first published in 1991; the page numbering belongs to the 1992 Simon & Schuster (Fireside) edition that Wikiquote cites.

trail: Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ for Awaken the Giant Within prints this sentence and cites page 75. We read the page’s raw wikitext rather than a summary, so the wording and the page number are as Wikiquote states them.

The edition history checks out independently: the Internet Archive catalogue record ↗ gives “New York: Simon & Schuster, 1992,” 552 pages, 1st Fireside edition, and notes it was “originally published: New York : Summit Books, c1991” — which is why this page dates the work to 1991 and the pagination to 1992.

Limit of what we checked: the page location rests on Wikiquote’s citation. The Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted and Google Books returned a bot challenge, so we did not confirm page 75 against the book’s own text.

author.bio: Born Anthony J. Mahavorić in North Hollywood, California, Robbins has worked as a speaker and coach since the late 1970s. He is best known for his large-scale seminars and for two early self-help books, Unlimited Power (1986) and Awaken the Giant Within (1991), which are the source of most of the sentences quoted under his name.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Robbins is not being inspirational here so much as stating the premise the rest of the chapter runs on: a belief is a mechanism with consequences, and it works in both directions.
The half that travels sounds like a motivational poster. The sentence immediately after it is the one doing the work, and it is about meaning-making rather than willpower.
detailsBody: Awaken the Giant Within runs to about 550 pages, and the lines quoted from it are almost always single sentences taken from the opening of a paragraph. That is worth knowing before trusting any short Robbins quotation: the attribution is usually sound, and the sentence is usually only part of what he wrote.
context.pull: A belief is a mechanism, and it cuts both ways.
